education.title: Education
education.intro: Master vocabulary for essays on academic systems, student life, teaching methods, and educational policies—essential for IELTS Writing Task 1 and 2.

words.def: the method and practice of teaching; the science of education
words.ex: Modern pedagogy emphasizes student-centered learning rather than rote memorization.

words.def: the subjects and courses offered by an educational institution
words.ex: The national curriculum was updated to include digital literacy skills.

words.def: official recognition that an institution meets established standards
words.ex: The university sought international accreditation to boost its reputation globally.

words.def: educational technique where teachers provide temporary support to help students learn
words.ex: Through scaffolding, the teacher gradually reduces hints as students gain confidence.

words.def: competence or skill level in a particular subject or language
words.ex: Students must demonstrate proficiency in English before entering university.

words.def: to register as a student at an educational institution
words.ex: Over 5,000 students enrolled in online courses this academic year.

words.def: something required as a prior condition before advancement
words.ex: Advanced Mathematics is a prerequisite for the Engineering degree.

words.def: to teach and instill values, habits, or ideas through repeated instruction
words.ex: Schools aim to inculcate critical thinking skills from an early age.

words.def: a fixed regular allowance or sum of money given to a student
words.ex: Merit scholars receive a monthly stipend to support their studies.

words.def: a group of students beginning their studies together in the same year
words.ex: The 2024 cohort of medical students is the largest in the university's history.

words.def: the fee charged for teaching or instruction, especially at a school or university
words.ex: Rising tuition fees have made higher education less accessible to low-income families.

words.def: to spread or distribute information, knowledge, or ideas widely
words.ex: Universities disseminate research findings through academic journals and conferences.

words.def: competence or skill level in a particular subject or language
words.ex: Teachers assess language proficiency through standardized tests.

words.def: the gradual reduction in numbers as people leave without replacement
words.ex: High student attrition rates indicate problems with course quality or support services.

words.def: a course or subject that students can choose rather than being required to take
words.ex: After completing core subjects, students must select three electives for their final year.

words.def: activities, programs, or learning outside the standard curriculum
words.ex: Participation in extracurricular activities develops social skills and leadership.

words.def: considering the whole system or person rather than individual parts
words.ex: A holistic approach to education develops students' emotional and social abilities alongside academics.

words.def: a person who evaluates or judges the performance or ability of someone
words.ex: Independent assessors evaluate student work to ensure fair and consistent grading.

words.def: a document or certificate that proves someone's qualifications or authority
words.ex: Teaching credentials are required before someone can work in schools.

words.def: structured in independent units or modules that can be taken separately
words.ex: The modular degree system allows students to study units in any order.

technology.title: Technology
technology.intro: Essential vocabulary for discussing innovation, digitalization, AI, and technological impact—critical for modern IELTS discussions and Writing Task 2 essays.

words.def: the introduction of new ideas, methods, or technologies
words.ex: Continuous innovation in software development improves user experience.

words.def: no longer in use or no longer useful; outdated
words.ex: Floppy disks became obsolete with the rise of cloud storage.

words.def: a step-by-step procedure or formula for solving a problem or performing a computation
words.ex: Search engine algorithms determine which websites appear first in results.

words.def: the use of machines or systems to perform tasks with minimal human intervention
words.ex: Factory automation has increased productivity but displaced many workers.

words.def: the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a connection
words.ex: High-bandwidth internet enables seamless video streaming and cloud computing.

words.def: protection of computer systems and networks from digital attacks and theft
words.ex: Strong cybersecurity measures are essential to protect personal data from hackers.

words.def: a sudden, usually temporary malfunction or problem in a system
words.ex: A software glitch caused the website to crash during peak hours.

words.def: the point of interaction between a user and a device or system
words.ex: User-friendly interfaces make technology accessible to non-technical people.

words.def: to combine or incorporate different systems or elements into a unified whole
words.ex: Companies integrate artificial intelligence into their business processes.

words.def: delay in data transmission or system response time
words.ex: Low latency is crucial for online gaming and real-time communication.

words.def: to use something to maximum advantage; to apply technology strategically
words.ex: Businesses leverage social media to reach wider audiences efficiently.

words.def: a set of rules governing data transmission or communication between systems
words.ex: Internet protocols ensure devices can communicate regardless of their type.

words.def: the ability to recover quickly from difficulties or adapt to change
words.ex: Infrastructure resilience ensures services continue during natural disasters.

words.def: the ability of a system to handle increased demand or growth
words.ex: Cloud computing offers excellent scalability for growing businesses.

words.def: smooth and without interruption or problems
words.ex: Cross-platform integration creates a seamless user experience.

words.def: close observation or monitoring of people, places, or systems
words.ex: CCTV surveillance has raised privacy concerns in many cities.

words.def: the creation of virtual versions of computing resources like servers or storage
words.ex: Virtualization reduces hardware costs and improves server efficiency.

words.def: a distributed digital ledger recording transactions across multiple computers
words.ex: Blockchain technology ensures transparency and security in cryptocurrency.

words.def: belonging exclusively to a particular company; not open-source
words.ex: Proprietary software restricts users from modifying or sharing the code.

words.def: the process of putting a system or application into active use
words.ex: The deployment of the new software required extensive staff training.

environment.title: Environment
environment.intro: Critical vocabulary for environmental issues, climate change, and sustainability—essential for IELTS Task 2 essays on pollution, conservation, and ecological challenges.

words.def: the total amount of greenhouse gases produced by human activities
words.ex: Reducing personal carbon footprint requires changes in transportation and consumption habits.

words.def: the variety of different plant and animal species in an environment
words.ex: Tropical rainforests contain 50% of Earth's biodiversity.

words.def: able to be maintained or continued without depleting natural resources
words.ex: Sustainable agriculture protects soil health for future generations.

words.def: capable of being replenished or regenerated naturally
words.ex: Solar and wind power are renewable energy sources unlike fossil fuels.

words.def: the clearing, removal, or destruction of forests
words.ex: Deforestation in Southeast Asia threatens countless endangered species.

words.def: a substance that contaminates air, water, or soil
words.ex: Industrial pollutants from factories damage aquatic ecosystems.

words.def: actions taken to reduce the severity or impact of something harmful
words.ex: Climate change mitigation requires transitioning away from coal energy.

words.def: a community of organisms and their physical environment functioning together
words.ex: Wetland ecosystems provide crucial habitats for migratory birds.

words.def: the process of becoming worse in quality or value; deterioration
words.ex: Land degradation from overgrazing reduces agricultural productivity.

words.def: the protection and preservation of natural resources and wildlife
words.ex: Conservation efforts have saved species like the giant panda from extinction.

words.def: the discharge or release of gases, particles, or radiation into the environment
words.ex: Vehicle emissions are a major source of urban air pollution.

words.def: the state of being insufficient in quantity; lack of something needed
words.ex: Water scarcity affects over 2 billion people worldwide.

words.def: to collect and reprocess waste materials into new products
words.ex: Recycling programs reduce landfill waste and conserve natural resources.

words.def: the presence of unwanted or harmful substances in an environment
words.ex: Soil contamination from chemical spills requires expensive remediation.

words.def: the natural environment where an organism or species lives
words.ex: Loss of habitat is the primary threat to endangered species.

words.def: the capacity of an ecosystem to recover from disturbances
words.ex: Coral reef resilience decreases with rising ocean temperatures.

words.def: the reduction in quantity or exhaustion of a resource
words.ex: Overfishing causes depletion of fish stocks in many oceans.

words.def: a chemical substance used to kill insects, weeds, or other organisms
words.ex: Excessive pesticide use harms non-target species and pollutes groundwater.

words.def: the effect of human activities on the natural environment
words.ex: Large infrastructure projects must undergo environmental impact assessments.

words.def: achieving a state where greenhouse gas emissions are balanced by removals
words.ex: Several countries aim to become carbon neutral by 2050.

health.title: Health
health.intro: Essential health-related vocabulary for discussing wellness, disease, medical treatment, and lifestyle—important for IELTS discussions and health-themed essays.

words.def: designed to stop something harmful from happening before it occurs
words.ex: Preventive healthcare emphasizes regular checkups and vaccinations.

words.def: the identification of an illness or condition based on symptoms and tests
words.ex: Early diagnosis of cancer significantly improves treatment outcomes.

words.def: therapy or treatment to restore function after injury or illness
words.ex: Physical rehabilitation helps stroke patients regain mobility.

words.def: a disease spreading rapidly among many people in a population
words.ex: The obesity epidemic affects children and adults in developed nations.

words.def: characterized by much sitting and little physical activity
words.ex: Sedentary lifestyles increase risks of heart disease and diabetes.

words.def: the process of making someone immune to disease through vaccination
words.ex: Childhood immunization programs have eradicated diseases like polio.

words.def: lasting a long time; of a disease persistent and long-lasting
words.ex: Chronic conditions like diabetes require ongoing medical management.

words.def: lack of proper nutrition or vitamins causing poor health
words.ex: Malnutrition affects millions of children in developing countries.

words.def: relating to the chemical processes that keep organisms alive
words.ex: Metabolic disorders affect how the body processes food for energy.

words.def: a sign or indication of disease or illness in a person
words.ex: Fever and cough are common symptoms of respiratory infections.

words.def: a disease outbreak affecting very large geographical areas and populations
words.ex: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare systems worldwide.

words.def: the number of deaths in a population within a specific time period
words.ex: Infant mortality rates have declined significantly in most developed countries.

words.def: relating to healing or treatment of disease or psychological problems
words.ex: Therapeutic exercises help manage chronic pain conditions.

words.def: a prediction of the likely course or outcome of a disease
words.ex: The prognosis for early-stage cancer treatment is generally favorable.

words.def: the science of drugs and their effects on living organisms
words.ex: Advances in pharmacology have created new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.

words.def: an approach treating the whole person including physical, mental, and social aspects
words.ex: Holistic health practices combine conventional medicine with wellness therapies.

words.def: a scientist who studies the spread and control of diseases
words.ex: Epidemiologists track disease patterns to prevent future outbreaks.

words.def: the simultaneous presence of two or more diseases in one person
words.ex: Diabetes and hypertension often occur together as a comorbidity.

words.def: a research study testing medical treatments on volunteer participants
words.ex: New medicines must complete clinical trials before approval.

words.def: groups at higher risk of health problems due to social or biological factors
words.ex: The elderly and immunocompromised are vulnerable populations during pandemics.

work.title: Work & Career
work.intro: Professional vocabulary for discussing employment, job responsibilities, workplace culture, and career development—essential for IELTS speaking and writing on work-related topics.

words.def: the ability to perform a job or task successfully and effectively
words.ex: Technical competency in programming languages is crucial for software engineers.

words.def: the assignment of responsibility or authority to another person
words.ex: Effective delegation allows managers to focus on strategic decisions.

words.def: a person who starts and operates their own business venture
words.ex: Successful entrepreneurs often take calculated risks to build their companies.

words.def: the process of integrating new employees and familiarizing them with the company
words.ex: A structured onboarding program helps new employees become productive quickly.

words.def: a formal review of an employee's job performance and conduct
words.ex: Annual performance appraisals help identify areas for professional development.

words.def: working together with others toward a common goal
words.ex: Cross-team collaboration improves project outcomes and innovation.

words.def: an experienced person who advises and guides a less experienced individual
words.ex: A good mentor provides career guidance and shares valuable industry insights.

words.def: dismissal from employment due to job elimination or business needs
words.ex: Factory redundancies increased as manufacturing moved overseas.

words.def: working for multiple employers without a permanent position
words.ex: Many professionals freelance to maintain flexible working schedules.

words.def: representation of different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives in the workplace
words.ex: Workplace diversity fosters creativity and improves decision-making.

words.def: advancement to a higher position with increased responsibility and salary
words.ex: Promotions are typically based on performance and years of service.

words.def: the journey between home and workplace; to travel regularly to work
words.ex: Remote work eliminates the daily commute for many employees.

words.def: a formal complaint about treatment or working conditions
words.ex: Employees can file a grievance if they believe their rights have been violated.

words.def: the effectiveness of effort as measured by work accomplished
words.ex: Flexible working hours improved employee productivity and satisfaction.

words.def: physical and emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged workplace stress
words.ex: Burnout rates among healthcare workers have reached critical levels.

words.def: building professional relationships to exchange information and opportunities
words.ex: Professional networking at conferences opens doors to new career opportunities.

words.def: a collection of competencies and abilities a person possesses
words.ex: Project managers require a diverse skill set including leadership and communication.

words.def: relating to a trial period to test suitability for employment
words.ex: New hires typically undergo a three-month probationary period.

words.def: payment or compensation for work or services provided
words.ex: Competitive remuneration packages attract top talent to the organization.

words.def: equilibrium between time spent on work and personal/family life
words.ex: Achieving work-life balance is crucial for long-term employee wellbeing.

crime.title: Crime & Law
crime.intro: Legal and criminal justice vocabulary for essays on law enforcement, punishment, rehabilitation, and social issues—important for IELTS Task 2 opinion essays.

words.def: a person who commits a crime or illegal act
words.ex: Police worked to identify the perpetrators of the burglary.

words.def: a minor criminal offense less serious than a felony
words.ex: Shoplifting is typically classified as a misdemeanor.

words.def: the legal process of charging and trying someone for a crime
words.ex: The prosecution presented strong evidence of guilt to the jury.

words.def: the formal decision or judgment delivered by a court or jury
words.ex: The jury returned a guilty verdict after deliberating for three hours.

words.def: the process of reintegrating offenders into society and reforming their behavior
words.ex: Modern prisons emphasize rehabilitation over pure punishment.

words.def: the tendency of released prisoners to reoffend or return to crime
words.ex: High recidivism rates indicate ineffective rehabilitation programs.

words.def: to find not guilty or to declare innocent of a crime
words.ex: The defendant was acquitted due to lack of evidence.

words.def: the state of being imprisoned or confined in prison
words.ex: Long-term incarceration can hinder successful rehabilitation.

words.def: a serious crime punishable by imprisonment for more than one year
words.ex: Armed robbery is classified as a felony in most jurisdictions.

words.def: a person accused of or on trial for a crime
words.ex: The defendant pleaded not guilty to the charges.

words.def: a formal judgment that someone is guilty of a crime
words.ex: A criminal conviction can affect employment opportunities.

words.def: the conditional release of a prisoner before the end of their sentence
words.ex: He was released on parole after serving half his sentence.

words.def: the official power or authority to make legal decisions in an area
words.ex: The case falls under federal jurisdiction because it involves interstate commerce.

words.def: the formal process of assigning punishment after a guilty verdict
words.ex: Sentencing guidelines help ensure consistent punishment across cases.

words.def: evidence given by a witness in court under oath
words.ex: The victim's testimony was crucial to securing a conviction.

words.def: a person who helps another commit a crime
words.ex: The accomplice was sentenced to five years imprisonment.

words.def: the act of taking something without permission with intent to keep it
words.ex: Identity theft has become increasingly common in the digital age.

words.def: a physical or verbal attack on another person
words.ex: Assault charges were filed following the altercation.

words.def: relating to scientific methods used in criminal investigations
words.ex: Forensic evidence such as DNA proved the suspect's guilt.

words.def: the network of courts and legal procedures for administering justice
words.ex: A fair and independent judicial system is essential for rule of law.

globalisation.title: Globalisation & Culture
globalisation.intro: Vocabulary for discussing international trade, cultural exchange, global movements, and cross-cultural issues—essential for IELTS essays on globalization impact.

words.def: the process of making different things similar or uniform
words.ex: Cultural homogenization threatens the preservation of indigenous traditions.

words.def: a group of people dispersed from their homeland living in foreign countries
words.ex: The Indian diaspora maintains strong cultural connections across continents.

words.def: the process of adapting to and becoming part of a different culture
words.ex: Assimilation of immigrants varies depending on community integration efforts.

words.def: a formal arrangement between countries to reduce tariffs and facilitate commerce
words.ex: International trade agreements have lowered barriers to global commerce.

words.def: operating in or involving multiple countries
words.ex: Multinational corporations influence economies and employment worldwide.

words.def: linked together; dependent on each other in relationships
words.ex: Global supply chains are highly interconnected, making economies vulnerable.

words.def: the practice of using external companies to perform business functions
words.ex: Manufacturing outsourcing to Asia reduced production costs significantly.

words.def: the mutual sharing of cultural elements between different societies
words.ex: International student programs promote cultural exchange and understanding.

words.def: the policy of extending a country's control over other territories
words.ex: Historical imperialism shaped political boundaries and cultures worldwide.

words.def: the right of a nation to govern itself without external interference
words.ex: Global treaties sometimes require countries to compromise national sovereignty.

words.def: a raw material or product traded on global markets
words.ex: Oil is a crucial commodity affecting global economic stability.

words.def: adaptation of products or services to local culture and preferences
words.ex: Successful localization requires understanding regional consumer preferences.

words.def: movement of people from one country or region to another
words.ex: Economic migration drives population changes in developing regions.

words.def: fear or hatred of foreigners and foreign cultures
words.ex: Rising xenophobia threatens social cohesion in multicultural societies.

words.def: a tax imposed on imported or exported goods
words.ex: Trade wars involve imposing steep tariffs on imported products.

words.def: the network of organizations involved in producing and delivering goods
words.ex: COVID-19 disrupted global supply chains affecting product availability.

words.def: efforts to maintain and protect traditional cultures and heritage
words.ex: UNESCO supports cultural preservation of endangered languages and traditions.

words.def: adaptation of global products to local markets and preferences
words.ex: Glocalization allows McDonald's to serve rice-based items in Asian markets.

words.def: a country with rapid economic growth and increasing investment opportunities
words.ex: India and Vietnam are considered emerging markets with huge growth potential.

words.def: the existence of different cultures and traditions within society
words.ex: Cultural diversity enriches communities and fosters innovation.

linking.title: Band 9 Linking Words & Phrases
linking.intro: Master discourse markers and connectors that elevate writing from Band 7 to Band 8-9—essential for coherence and cohesion in IELTS Writing and Speaking.

words.def: in addition; moreover; used to add information supporting the previous point
words.ex: Remote work improves flexibility. Furthermore, it reduces commuting costs.

words.def: as a result; therefore; showing cause-and-effect relationships
words.ex: Obesity is rising in developed nations. Consequently, health systems face increasing pressure.

words.def: on the other hand; in contrast; introducing opposing information
words.ex: Urban areas offer employment. Conversely, rural regions provide natural beauty.

words.def: in spite of that; however; used to show contrast
words.ex: Climate change is urgent. Nonetheless, many governments delay action.

words.def: in spite of; despite; used in formal writing
words.ex: Notwithstanding economic challenges, the company expanded operations.

words.def: afterwards; later; showing sequence of events
words.ex: The new policy was introduced in 2020. Subsequently, efficiency improved.

words.def: at the same time; during the same period
words.ex: Manufacturing declined in developed nations. Meanwhile, it grew in Asia.

words.def: in addition; furthermore; used to add supporting points
words.ex: Education improves employment prospects. Moreover, it enhances social mobility.

words.def: in the same way; similarly; indicating parallel ideas
words.ex: Western diets are unhealthy. Likewise, sedentary lifestyles cause disease.

words.def: showing a striking difference between two things
words.ex: Developed nations have low birth rates. In contrast, developing countries grow rapidly.

words.def: introducing the first of two contrasting points
words.ex: On the one hand, globalization creates opportunities. On the other, it threatens cultures.

words.def: it is true that; acknowledging a valid point before presenting counterargument
words.ex: Admittedly, technology disrupts employment. Nevertheless, it creates new jobs.

words.def: finally; in the end; introducing a conclusion
words.ex: Renewable energy requires investment. Ultimately, it benefits the environment.

words.def: especially; in particular; highlighting important information
words.ex: Many countries ban plastics. Notably, India implemented strict regulations.

words.def: however; in spite of that; introducing a contrasting statement
words.ex: The law is strict. Nevertheless, violations occur frequently.

words.def: considering; taking into account; introducing new context
words.ex: In light of climate data, urgent action is necessary.

words.def: considering everything; in summary; introducing final conclusion
words.ex: All in all, the benefits of technology outweigh the drawbacks.

words.def: to give an example; introducing specific evidence
words.ex: Education improves quality of life. To illustrate, university graduates earn more.

words.def: it is true; acknowledging a valid point in an argument
words.ex: Granted, automation reduces jobs. However, efficiency gains benefit consumers.

words.def: finally; at the end; introducing a summary statement
words.ex: In conclusion, sustainable development requires global cooperation.

toefl.title: TOEFL High-Frequency Academic Words
toefl.intro: Academic vocabulary essential for TOEFL reading, listening, and writing sections—word families commonly tested in university-level English proficiency exams.

words.def: to examine something carefully by breaking it into components
words.ex: Students must analyze historical texts to understand social trends.

words.def: existing in thought or theory; not concrete or physical
words.ex: Philosophy deals with abstract concepts like justice and morality.

words.def: to obtain or gain something through effort or purchase
words.ex: Students acquire knowledge through reading and classroom participation.

words.def: lying near or next to something; adjoining
words.ex: The library is adjacent to the student center on campus.

words.def: to support or recommend; a person who supports a cause
words.ex: Environmental groups advocate for stricter pollution controls.

words.def: to distribute or assign resources for a specific purpose
words.ex: The university allocates funding to different departments annually.

words.def: having more than one possible interpretation; unclear
words.ex: The statement was ambiguous, leading to different understandings.

words.def: occurring once every year; yearly
words.ex: The annual conference brings together scientists from worldwide.

words.def: to expect or predict something will happen
words.ex: Researchers anticipate that technology will solve environmental problems.

words.def: clearly visible or obvious; seeming to be true
words.ex: It was apparent that the experiment had succeeded.

words.def: based on random choice rather than reason or system
words.ex: Setting arbitrary deadlines without justification frustrates students.

words.def: to express ideas clearly; able to speak clearly
words.ex: The speaker articulated complex ideas in simple language.

words.def: to believe something is true without proof; to take responsibility
words.ex: We cannot assume that all students have internet access.

words.def: to regard as caused by; a characteristic or quality
words.ex: Historians attribute the decline to economic factors.

words.def: power or right to make decisions; an expert
words.ex: Climate scientists have authority on environmental matters.

words.def: an advantage or favorable result; to gain advantage
words.ex: Students benefit from attending lectures and studying independently.

words.def: prejudice or favoritism; inclination toward something
words.ex: Research must minimize bias to produce valid results.

words.def: to quote or refer to as evidence or authority
words.ex: Academic papers must cite sources to support claims.

words.def: logically organized and clearly connected; easy to understand
words.ex: A coherent argument presents ideas in logical sequence.

words.def: to be a part of; to make up or form something
words.ex: Students constitute the majority of campus residents.
